module.purpose: Provides the React container that selects a DevTools monitor, initializes monitor-specific state, and renders it with Redux state, feature flags, theme, and state-tree settings.
module.summary: This container dynamically resolves a monitor component from application properties and coordinates its optional update lifecycle with Redux dispatching. It suppresses one render when monitor initialization produces a state change, avoids unnecessary updates through prop comparison, and injects lifted state, monitor properties, theme, feature controls, and dispatch behavior into the selected monitor.
module.businessContext: This file powers the Redux DevTools user interface by connecting configured monitors to application state. If it fails, monitor visualization, state inspection, and monitor-specific controls cannot render or initialize correctly.

units.name: getMonitor

detail.name: getMonitor
preconditions: props is a valid Props value accepted by getMonitor.
postconditions: this.monitorProps is set to the resolved monitor element's props.
this.Monitor is set to the resolved monitor element's type.
When the resolved monitor exposes update, this.dispatch is called with type '@@INIT_MONITOR', the selected monitor state, the update function, and the resolved monitor props.
When monitor update produces a state different from props.monitorState, this.preventRender is set to true.
invariants: The dispatched monitorProps value is the same value assigned to this.monitorProps.
The dispatched update value is the resolved monitor type's update function.
A truthy skipUpdate or a monitor state whose __overwritten__ value equals props.monitor causes the existing props.monitorState to be dispatched without invoking update.
edgeCases: If the resolved monitor type has no update function, monitor selection fields are updated but no monitor initialization dispatch occurs.
If skipUpdate is truthy, props.monitorState is used directly and the monitor update function is not invoked.
If props.monitorState.__overwritten__ equals props.monitor, props.monitorState is used directly and the monitor update function is not invoked.
If update returns a value different from props.monitorState, this.preventRender is set to true before dispatch.
If update returns the same value as props.monitorState, this.preventRender is not set by this method.
stateMutations: this.preventRender when monitor update returns a state different from props.monitorState
detail.summary: Resolves the monitor element from the supplied props, updates the active monitor type and props, and initializes the monitor state through dispatch. It reuses an existing or overwritten monitor state when applicable and prevents rendering when monitor initialization produces a different state.

specLiterals.role: Dispatched action type used to initialize the monitor.

specTests.when: getMonitor(props) is called and the update function returns a state different from props.monitorState.
specTests.then: The monitor props and type are stored, this.preventRender becomes true, and this.dispatch receives an '@@INIT_MONITOR' action containing the returned state, update function, and monitor props.
props.monitorState is dispatched as newMonitorState and the monitor update function is not invoked.

units.name: shouldComponentUpdate

detail.name: shouldComponentUpdate
preconditions: nextProps conforms to the Props shape.
nextProps.theme is present and has a scheme property.
postconditions: Returns a boolean indicating whether the component should update.
Returns true if monitor, liftedState, monitorState, features, or theme.scheme differs from the current props; otherwise returns false.
invariants: The current component props are not mutated.
The decision is based on strict inequality comparisons of the monitored values.
edgeCases: When all monitored values are strictly equal between nextProps and the current props, returns false.
When any one of monitor, liftedState, monitorState, features, or theme.scheme is strictly different, returns true.
Changes to props not included in the monitored comparisons do not affect the returned decision.
detail.summary: Determines whether the DevTools component should re-render when receiving new props. It returns true when any monitored prop or the theme scheme changes.

units.name: render

detail.name: render
preconditions: this.props contains liftedState, monitorState, monitor, features, theme, and stateTreeSettings values.
this.Monitor references the monitor component to render.
postconditions: If this.preventRender is true on entry, it is set to false and the method returns null.

Otherwise, the method returns a div whose className identifies the monitor and whose child monitor receives the assembled state, monitor properties, feature settings, dispatch callback, theme, and state-tree settings.
invariants: The rendered monitor receives monitorState from this.props.monitorState in the lifted-state props.
The rendered wrapper className has the form "monitor monitor-${this.props.monitor}".
edgeCases: When preventRender is true, no monitor wrapper is rendered, preventRender is reset to false, and null is returned.
When preventRender is false, the monitor is rendered inside a div even if prop values are falsey; those values are passed through to the child monitor.
stateMutations: Sets this.preventRender from true to false when rendering is suppressed.
